title: Police Form Multiple Teams to Nab Suspects in Odisha Gang Rape Case
excerpt: A woman was allegedly gang-raped by a group of men in Cuttack district while out on a drive with a friend. A DSP-rank officer has been appointed to lead the investigation.
body:
• A woman was allegedly gang-raped by a group of four to six men in Odisha's Cuttack district on Tuesday night
  • Police have registered a case and appointed a DSP-rank officer to lead the investigation
  • Multiple teams have been deployed to track down and arrest the suspects, who fled the scene
  • The incident occurred near Sukarpada village on the Cuttack-Chandbali Road in the Nischintakoili area

Police in Odisha's Cuttack district have launched a manhunt for a group of men accused of gang-raping a woman on Tuesday night while she was traveling with a male friend, officials said on Wednesday.

The incident took place in the Nischintakoili police station area, according to SP (Cuttack Rural) Vinit Agrawal. The woman and her companion were traveling from Bhubaneswar toward Kendrapara when they stopped near Sukarpada village on the Cuttack-Chandbali Road.

What Happened

According to police, a group of four to six men intercepted the pair after they stopped along the road. The group allegedly assaulted the woman's male companion before sexually assaulting her. The attackers fled the scene, leaving the two behind, Agrawal said.

Police registered a case based on the woman's complaint filed at the Nischintakoili police station. A DSP-rank officer has been appointed to lead the investigation, indicating the priority authorities are assigning to the case.

Investigation Underway

"Multiple teams have been formed to nab the accused. We are hopeful that they will be arrested soon."

— Vinit Agrawal, SP, Cuttack Rural

Agrawal confirmed that several teams have been deployed across the district to identify and apprehend the suspects. Police are examining evidence from the scene and pursuing leads in the Nischintakoili area and surrounding villages as part of the investigation.

The case has drawn attention to safety concerns on rural stretches of Odisha's highways, particularly on less-patrolled road corridors after dark. The Cuttack-Chandbali Road connects several semi-urban towns and sees regular traffic between Bhubaneswar and the coastal districts.

Legal Framework

Under Indian criminal law, gang rape cases carry a minimum sentence of 20 years imprisonment, which can extend to life imprisonment. Cases involving aggravated circumstances can attract even stricter penalties under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the criminal code that replaced the Indian Penal Code in 2024.

Odisha has in recent years strengthened its police response mechanisms for crimes against women, including the establishment of dedicated women's police stations and fast-track courts for sexual assault cases. The state government has also expanded CCTV coverage on major highways and increased patrolling on vulnerable stretches.

What's Next

With a DSP-rank officer heading the investigation and multiple teams in the field, police say they are confident of making arrests soon. Authorities have urged anyone with information about the incident or the suspects to contact local police. The investigation is ongoing.
